programs.title: Cloud & Systems Engineering
programs.description: Build from packets, operating systems, and identity into cloud platforms, automation, observability, Kubernetes, and recovery engineering.
prerequisites: Basic computer literacy; no prior cloud certification required
Comfort using a terminal becomes useful after the foundation modules
outcomes: Trace a request across DNS, networks, transport, TLS, applications, and infrastructure
Administer Linux/Windows and identity concepts using evidence-based troubleshooting
Design cloud and Kubernetes systems around failure, observability, automation, and recovery
Explain tradeoffs among availability, security, cost, performance, and operational complexity
programs.capstone: Design and defend a resilient service architecture, then reproduce at least one failure/recovery scenario with preserved evidence.

programs.title: Advanced Computing
programs.description: Connect computer architecture, operating systems, memory, parallelism, distributed systems, GPU computing, HPC, and quantum computing.
prerequisites: Basic algebra; linear algebra becomes increasingly important
Operating-system and networking fundamentals recommended for distributed/HPC work
outcomes: Reason about compute from processor/memory architecture through distributed execution
Model performance, parallelism, locality, synchronization, and failure
Explain GPU/HPC design tradeoffs and measurement methodology
Separate quantum-computing mathematics, simulation, hardware claims, and experimental evidence
programs.capstone: Choose an advanced-computing workload, identify its computational bottleneck, build a reproducible model, and defend the architecture and measurement plan.

programs.title: Software Engineering
programs.description: Learn programming, data structures, algorithms, APIs, databases, testing, architecture, DevOps, and production software reasoning.
prerequisites: Basic programming concepts are recommended before advanced architecture modules
outcomes: Translate requirements into testable software behavior
Choose data structures and algorithms from constraints rather than habit
Design APIs, data models, tests, and failure handling as explicit contracts
Ship software through version control, CI/CD, observability, and reversible change
programs.capstone: Build a small service with a documented contract, persistent data, automated tests, failure handling, and a reproducible delivery path.

programs.title: Cybersecurity
programs.description: Learn security foundations, identity, risk, network and application security, endpoint defense, detection, governance, recovery, and secure architecture.
prerequisites: Networking and operating-system fundamentals are strongly recommended
All practical exercises must use owned, isolated, synthetic, or explicitly authorized systems
outcomes: Model assets, trust boundaries, threats, controls, and residual risk
Evaluate identity, network, endpoint, application, and cloud security controls
Reproduce vulnerabilities safely and connect findings to remediation and detection
Communicate security evidence using repeatable methods and explicit authorization boundaries
programs.capstone: Complete an authorized security assessment of a synthetic environment: threat model, reproduce a bounded weakness, remediate it, and verify the control.

programs.title: Technical Leadership & IT Management
programs.description: Develop operational leadership across incidents, ITSM, teams, strategy, projects, vendors, governance, risk, finance, capacity, reliability, and recovery.
prerequisites: Some workplace or project experience is helpful but not required
outcomes: Translate technical conditions into operational and business decisions
Run incidents, projects, services, vendors, and teams with explicit ownership and evidence
Reason about reliability, capacity, cost, risk, and governance together
Communicate decisions, assumptions, uncertainty, and follow-through clearly
programs.capstone: Lead a simulated service review from incident evidence through risk, budget, ownership, reliability work, and an executive decision memo.

programs.title: Mathematics for Engineering & Computing
programs.description: Build algebraic fluency into functions, discrete math, sequences, trigonometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, and numerical methods.
prerequisites: Arithmetic and basic algebra are enough to begin
Calculus and linear algebra paths provide their own prerequisite bridges
outcomes: Represent technical problems with equations, functions, vectors, matrices, graphs, and probability
Derive results instead of relying only on memorized formulas
Check calculations numerically and interpret assumptions and error
Connect mathematics to software, physics, AI, networks, and advanced computing
programs.capstone: Model a real engineering question mathematically, derive an expected result, compute it independently, and explain the limits of the model.

programs.title: Physics for Engineers
programs.description: Develop mechanics, momentum, rotation, energy, waves, thermodynamics, electricity, magnetism, modern physics, and quantum foundations through models and experiments.
prerequisites: Algebra required; trigonometry and calculus become useful as the course deepens
outcomes: Translate physical situations into models with units, assumptions, and conservation laws
Solve and verify mechanics, energy, wave, electricity, magnetism, and thermodynamic problems
Distinguish idealized models from experimental systems and measurement uncertainty
Connect modern/quantum physics to engineering and computing without overstating what a model proves
programs.capstone: Design a bounded physics investigation with prediction, model, measurement or simulation, uncertainty discussion, and evidence-backed conclusion.
